patent: European patent application by Hitachi, Ltd. (inventors Tatenori Jinriki and Fusaaki Kozawa), filed 1986-04-29 with Japanese priority of 1985-04-30, published 1986-11-05, designating DE, FR and GB. This application was never granted: Google Patents lists it as withdrawn 1988-06-22, event published 1988-08-17 (checked 2026-11-02), and lists a family member US 4,696,202. The embodiment is a three-member robot wrist with all three motors at the rear of the fore arm. Power reaches the wrist through nested drive shafts and double universal joints, then reduction gears, one of which (28) is described as similar in structure to a HARMONIC DRIVE gear. Each wrist member turns about its own axis, at a fixed angle to the previous one, rather than bending, so the angle across each universal joint does not change as the wrist moves. No link to a Hitachi product is claimed here.

glossary.def: The patent's name for the cross, or spider, at the center of a Cardan joint. Its two pin axes connect the two yokes.
Also Hooke's joint, the common universal joint. At a nonzero joint angle a constant input speed gives an output speed that fluctuates within each revolution.
Two Cardan joints in series on an intermediate shaft. Equal joint angles and correct phasing cancel the fluctuation between the outer shafts. Each composite joint here is of this kind.
Robotics term, not used in the patent, for a wrist of three successive rotary joints with mutually inclined axes, with no joint that bends. In this embodiment the axes do not all meet at one point.

Generic name for HARMONIC DRIVE gearing, invented by C. Walton Musser in the 1950s. An oval wave generator flexes a thin toothed ring into a rigid ring with slightly more teeth, giving a high ratio in one stage with little backlash.
Free play between meshing gear teeth, felt as lost motion when the drive reverses.
Screw and nut running on recirculating balls. Here it also works as a rotating shaft: the nut's travel measures the turns of the drive.
Linear ball bearing, a sleeve that slides along a round shaft on balls.
In current usage, a vertically articulated robot arm with a waist, shoulder and elbow.
